question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹44, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct relation between Principal (P), 1-year SI and CI-SI difference for 2 years:

P = (1-year SI)² ÷ Difference

1-year SI = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

Difference (CI − SI) = 44 − 40 = ₹4

P = 20² ÷ 4 = 400 ÷ 4 = ₹100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest for 2 years (SI) = ₹40

Compound Interest for 2 years (CI) = ₹44

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

SI for 1 year = Total SI ÷ 2

Difference between 2 years CI and SI = Interest on 1st year's SI

Rate (R) = (Difference ÷ 1st year SI) × 100

Principal = (1st year SI × 100) ÷ Rate

 Interest on Year 1 SI = ₹4

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 1 year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

⇒ Difference between CI and SI = 44 − 40 = ₹4

⇒ In Compound Interest, the difference of ₹4 is the interest generated on the 1st year's SI (₹20).

⇒ Rate (R) = (4 ÷ 20) × 100 = 20%

⇒ We know, SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ Applying for 1 year: 20 = (P × 20 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (20 × 100) ÷ 20

⇒ P = ₹100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between 2 Years CI and SI

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years on a principal P at rate R% is given by the formula: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Difference between 3 Years CI and SI

For 3 years, the difference formula is: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)² × (300 + R) ÷ 100.

Relationship between CI and SI

For the first year, Simple Interest (SI) and Compound Interest (CI) are always equal, provided the interest is calculated annually.
